info.desc: Out of Time is the seventh album by the American alternative rock band R.E.M., released on Warner Bros. Records in 1991. With Out of Time R.E.M.'s status grew from that of a cult band to a massive international act. The record topped the album sales charts in both the U.S. and the United Kingdom, spending 109 weeks on American album charts and enjoying two separate spells at the summit, and 183 weeks on the British charts, and spending a single week at the top. The album has been certified four times platinum in the U.S. and sold over ten million .

podcast.body: Released on March 12, 1991, this album transformed R.E.M. from a cult band into major international stars. It spent 109 weeks on the US charts and 183 weeks on the UK charts, reaching number one in the US, Britain, Canada, France, the Netherlands, and Italy, and top five in Australia, New Zealand, Norway, Sweden, and Switzerland. With nearly 5 million worldwide sales, it won three Grammy Awards the following February, including Best Alternative Album. "Out of time is the record that turned R.E.M. from a cult band, a big cult band, but one nevertheless, into major international stars."

podcast.body: This album marked R.E.M.'s successful transition from a "left of the dial" college rock band to a mainstream powerhouse. Released in 1991, *Out of Time* achieved the number one spot on the album charts, demonstrating the marketability of "mainstream REM jangle" even as grunge began to dominate. "In 1991, their out-of-time was a number one album."
